'''Joan Elisabeth Adler''' ({{Langx|he|ג'ואן אדלר}}; born 1950) is a [[Computational physics|computational physicist]] at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]]. Originally from Australia, she is a citizen of both Australia and Israel. Her research involves [[percolation theory]], [[Lattice model (physics)|lattice models]], and [[neural network]]s.<ref name="cv">[http://phycomp.technion.ac.il/~phr76ja/vita/vitaup.pdf Curriculum vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209124002/http://phycomp.technion.ac.il/~phr76ja/vita/vitaup.pdf |date=2018-12-09  }}, accessed 2016-06-04.</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Adler was born on 13 June 1950 in [[Sydney]], Australia.
She graduated with a B.Sc. in mathematics and physics from the [[University of Sydney]] in 1974. She completed her doctorate in physics in 1980, at the [[University of New South Wales]]. 

== Career ==
She worked at the Technion from 1980 to 1984 as a postdoctoral fellow and research associate, returned as a senior research associate in 1988, and became a senior research fellow in 2000. She was president of the Israel Physical Society from 2005–2007.<ref name="cv" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Joan Adler {{!}} RBNI |url=https://rbni.technion.ac.il/node/190 |access-date=2022-07-29 |website=rbni.technion.ac.il}}</ref>

At Russell Berrie Nanotechnology Institute [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Technion–Israel Institute of Technology]] in Haifa, her recent research has included atomistic and electronic simulation and visualization for condensed matter and materials (including nanotubes), computational physics education, and statistical physics. She has also studied 3D stereo visualization for physics education and interopability of multiscale simulations.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Joan Adler - Physics Department, Technion |url=https://phys.technion.ac.il/en/people/emeriti/person/7 |access-date=2022-07-29 |website=phys.technion.ac.il}}</ref>

In 2005, Adler became a [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics|Fellow]] of the [[Institute of Physics]] (Great Britain).<ref name="cv" />

== Distinctions ==
* 1970–1973: Commonwealth Undergraduate Scholarship
* 1975–1978: Australian Postgraduate Research Award
* 1980–1983: Lady Davis Postdoctoral Fellowship
* 1987: PICS French-Israeli Travel Award

== Select publications ==
* Adler, Joan, [[Yigal Meir]], [[Amnon Aharony]], and A. Brooks Harris. "Series study of percolation moments in general dimension." ''Physical Review B'' 41, no. 13 (1990): 9183.
* Adler, Joan. "Bootstrap percolation." ''Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications'' 171, no. 3 (1991): 453-470.
* Hashibon, Adham, Joan Adler, Michael W. Finnis, and Wayne D. Kaplan. "Atomistic study of structural correlations at a liquid-solid interface." ''Computational materials science'' 24, no. 4 (2002): 443-452.
* Adler, Joan, and Uri Lev. "Bootstrap percolation: visualizations and applications." ''Brazilian Journal of Physics'' 33 (2003): 641-644.
